brief: One screen for five trustees, two minutes, whatever device is to hand
vision: Within two minutes a non-analyst leaves with a feeling: donations falling while demand rises. That reading is available before any chart is studied.
The one thing that is not all right — Pike Street, under a week of stock, nine volunteers — is findable without hunting, and is marked by form as well as by number.
Numbers that are compared are aligned and set in tabular figures, so the eye can compare them without arithmetic.
Any chart is drawn to a scale: labelled at values it reaches, with axes and marks clear of one another.
The screen is one screen. It has not become a six-section report.
code: Self-contained: no external stylesheet, script, font or image, and no charting library pulled from a CDN.
It does not throw. Nothing in the console at load.
At 375px the whole screen still works — this is a device the trustees may actually use, not a fallback.
The figures on the page come from the supplied data rather than being hard-coded copies that can drift from it.
Any chart is drawn with real elements or a canvas, with the values reachable in the DOM rather than baked into an image.
